beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

beats.heading: One application, one admission

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name

beats.heading: One application, one admission
beats.body: Every request enters the same composed application, and every change is admitted and counted until it settles, so a stop drains what it has accepted rather than lose it, or refuses with SERVER_BUSY and goes on serving.

beats.heading: Meaning is read once and drawn here
beats.body: A read answers with the board family or with a drawing made on the server. The browser is a viewer: it holds board content only as a read-only cache of what this said.

beats.heading: One write boundary, one lease
beats.body: Every change goes through one boundary: the writer states the version it read, the board's lease admits one writer at a time, and the file is committed before the write is answered.

beats.heading: A claim is visible wherever the board is
beats.body: When the holder of a board's lease changes, every pane showing the board is told who has it and what they said they were doing, and a person's one control is taking the claim back.

beats.heading: A rename carries what the server keyed by the name
beats.body: A rename is a write like any other, and then the panes on the board, the claim on it and what the agent said it was doing move to the new name. The old name stays a former name, so anything still using it reaches the board.

beats.heading: The file stays the truth while panes stay live
beats.body: A pane is told a new version exists and reads again; a change nobody here made is noticed on disk and announced the same way. The agent reads the same announcements as a feed with a cursor. Nothing about a board lives in a pane.

beats.heading: A tab keeps its conversation through a reload
beats.body: Each pane names its browser tab when its socket opens, and the close of that socket forgets it. When the last pane of a tab closes, the tab has 60 seconds to come back, so a reload keeps its conversation. After that, the Codex workbench ends the tab session.

nodes.name: Code check
nodes.responsibility: Holds each board's anchors, bound symbols, relationships between bound parts and container interfaces to the code facts of the files on disk, at its current variant or the named draft
nodes.description: ADR 0046's code pass. It reads the files Git does not ignore in each registered checkout through the code opener's checkout rules, asking code facts for each: a bound symbol must be a definition, and an anchor's symbol a definition or a use. It reports ANCHOR_PATH_MISSING, ANCHOR_SYMBOL_MISSING, BINDING_SYMBOL_MISSING, ANCHOR_MISMATCH for an anchor whose symbol is defined outside the bound code of both ends or whose uses are of an evidence kind the relationship kind does not accept and, on a named draft, BINDING_PATH_MISSING. From the code facts of every bound file it reads the evidence between the bound parts of each board, owned by the narrowest binding, a C or C++ file's part owning its pair where no part binds it: a use at run time reached through an import or an include is a call, a use only as a type an import. It reports RELATIONSHIP_UNDRAWN once on the part that code reaches with no relationship, RELATIONSHIP_BACKWARDS and RELATIONSHIP_UNSUPPORTED as information for a relationship with no anchor, judged by the evidence kinds the vault configuration lets its kind accept. For each container bound to a module, a directory or its index file, it holds the interface that ADR 0044 derives against what the module exposes, as code facts read it: ENTRY_POINT_UNEXPOSED for an entry point that owns nothing the module exposes while a drawn caller's code reaches it from outside the module, CALLER_UNDRAWN for a hidden part whose exposed code a file outside the module uses at run time where no part on the board owns that use, and EXPOSED_UNUSED, information, for exposed names no file outside the module uses. A module it cannot read is skipped as exposure-unknown. A binding to a Terraform root module names an address there (module-not-read in a remote module); references join resource-bound parts, and --plan names plan JSON files. A language server resolves the uses no import resolves. It lists what it skipped and why, such as a symbol found only in code that did not parse.

nodes.name: Code facts
nodes.responsibility: Tells the code check what one file defines, references and imports, and what a module exposes, and keeps each file's facts in memory by its content
nodes.description: ADR 0046's engine. A table of adapters names, for each language or format, the files it reads, how it reads them (tree-sitter, or a parser Bun has) and its import resolver. TypeScript and TSX: definitions qualified by what holds them; imports through the nearest tsconfig.json and the @/ alias. Python: module names and class members, exposed by __all__ or a name without _; absolute, relative and package imports against the file's root, the source roots of pyproject.toml or setup.cfg, and src. docker-compose (Bun.YAML): services, networks and volumes are definitions (services.web); depends_on, links, networks, named and shared volumes and environment values that name a service are configured paths, merged with the override in compose order; an env file gives names, never values. Nix: flake.nix read statically; each output is a definition by attribute path (packages.x86_64-linux.archboard), * standing for each system of a list it cannot read; names below what it cannot follow are unknown, never missing; each flake.lock input is a build dependency. C and C++: names qualified with ::, with C's visibility; an #include puts its header's names in scope, resolved through compile_commands.json or else relative paths; a header and its source file are a pair. Terraform and OpenTofu (.tf, .tofu): declarations by address (aws_sqs_queue.jobs, module.q.var.x for a call's argument) and each address an expression names; a root module is one address space across its local modules, a named plan JSON filling in remote ones. Swift: access levels; names resolve across a module and its imports; Package.swift, read statically, gives modules and build dependencies. References carry their evidence kind; environment values and events written as strings count. Code that did not parse holds no facts; other files are text. It finds a symbol's definition and what a module exposes. One cache entry per file, keyed on its bytes' hash; grammars load on first use; a pass yields after each parse.
